We built this to reduce our own frustrations with building an MCP/API for these agents to consume. The problem: testing against these tools is hard! Agent memory + account statefulness make reproducibility, in the ways required for repeatable/reliable outcomes, between agents and the APIs/MCPs they interact with very challenging. The solution: CATT lets devs test their services against a surrogate Muse or Instinct agent (not affiliated with either of these companies). Testers define starting conditions, approvals, and success conditions for their service's state. CATT then records the full interaction (incl. tool calls, responses) so it can diff what

items.title: Secure your AI agents on Mac
items.raw_excerpt:
Plango is a Mac native security suite for anyone running AI coding tools. It works by running a custom local security model that evaluates threats against the lethal trifecta (data access, communication, exposure). Some cool features:
- Restrict Agent access by type of data (ssh keys, env files) or finder tags (finally a good reason to use the color tags in finder).
- On device security model, but can switch to another local agent or bring your own key.
- Review your Mac's privacy and access, apps, startup & extensions.
- Automatically move env secrets into keychain.
- Network blocks/allow lists, see what apps and agents are accessing. Stop them from data exfil.
- Check skills and plugins for bad behavior.
- Create custom rules for all of these things.
- Log every action, request, block et

items.title: The Customer Is the Builder: how AI coding agents change software economics
items.raw_excerpt: AI coding agents could change whether organizations buy software or build the functionality they need. We focus on organizations and professional buyers whose domain knowledge can help them specify and evaluate tools for their work. We define the software substitution frontier as the functions customers could build and maintain at an acceptable standard for less than buying them. items.title: Making a smart TV dumb and then smart
items.raw_excerpt: A recent (unwanted) webOS update that got installed on TV prompted me to start going down the rabbit hole of writing new TV software. After a couple of weekends and massive help from 4 different models, finally managed to get v1 working. My daughter enjoys navigating TV through speech while I get to browse on the biggest screen at home. While all of the code was written by ML models, there were decisions I had to help with. In specific: using WebRTC to cut down latency, repurposing vendor logic for buffering voice samples and designing user experience. It was liberating to finally free the TV of bloatware and make it truly personalized!
